about.ex: The trip takes about two hours.

accounts.en: a company's written records of money
accounts.ex: The firm published its yearly accounts in March.

acquired.ex: The museum acquired a rare painting last year.

add.ex: Extra fees can add a lot to the bill.

agencies.en: government organisations with a special job
agencies.ex: Several agencies worked together after the flood.

also.ex: She speaks French and also some Spanish.

amid.en: during; while something else is happening

amounts.ex: We saved small amounts every month.

announced.ex: The school announced a new head teacher.

anticipate.ex: We anticipate heavy traffic over the holiday weekend.

example.en: We anticipate strong demand for the new model.
example.zh: 我們預期新款會有強勁需求。

note.usage: 後接名詞、動名詞或 that 子句；比 expect 正式。

noteEn.meaning: to expect that something will happen.
noteEn.usage: Followed by a noun, -ing or a that-clause; more formal than 'expect'.

noteEs.exampleTr: Prevemos una fuerte demanda del nuevo modelo.
noteEs.meaning: prever o esperar que algo ocurra.
noteEs.usage: Va con sustantivo, -ing o that; más formal que expect.

noteHi.exampleTr: हमें नए मॉडल की भारी माँग की उम्मीद है।
noteHi.meaning: पहले से अनुमान या उम्मीद करना कि कुछ होगा।
noteHi.usage: संज्ञा, -ing या that उपवाक्य के साथ; expect से अधिक औपचारिक।

noteJa.exampleTr: 新モデルには強い需要が見込まれる。
noteJa.meaning: 何かが起こると予期する。
noteJa.usage: 名詞・動名詞・that節を続ける。expect より硬い。

noteKo.exampleTr: 우리는 새 모델에 대한 수요가 클 것으로 예상한다.
noteKo.usage: 명사, 동명사, that절이 뒤따르며 expect보다 격식 있다.

apiece.ex: The tickets cost ten euro apiece.

approach.en: a way of dealing with something
approach.ex: We need a new approach to the problem.

approval.ex: The plan still needs council approval.

approximately.ex: The film lasts approximately ninety minutes.

arguments.ex: Their arguments about money lasted for years.

around.ex: Around fifty people came to the meeting.

as.en: because; also in "as much as" (up to)
as.zh: as much as：多達；（連接詞）因為

at.en: used for a place or point

ballooned.ex: Their phone bill ballooned during the holiday.

belonging.ex: The car belonging to my uncle is red.

big.ex: They live in a big house near the sea.

bodies.ex: Public bodies must publish their spending.

bought.ex: She bought a new bike last week.

bring.en: cause something to come to a place
bring.ex: The new road will bring more visitors.

building.en: making houses, roads and other structures

by.en: showing who does it or how much

call.ex: People call him the king of jazz.

case.en: a matter decided in a court
case.ex: The judge will hear the case next week.

cases.ex: In some cases, students can get free tickets.

cautionary.ex: His story is a cautionary tale about debt.
cautionary.zh: cautionary tale：警世故事；前車之鑑

challenge.en: a legal action questioning a decision
challenge.ex: The group lost its challenge to the new law.

challenged.en: formally questioned a decision in court
challenged.ex: Residents challenged the plan in court.

challenges.ex: Court challenges can take many years.

cheaper.ex: Trains are cheaper than taxis here.

comes.ex: Buying in bulk often comes cheaper.

commence.ex: The ceremony will commence at noon.

company.en: a business that sells goods or services
company.ex: My sister works for a large company.

company's.ex: The company's profits rose this year.

comparable.ex: Prices here are comparable to last year's.

concern.ex: There is growing concern about rising rents.

confidential.ex: The details of the deal remain confidential.

example.en: Please keep these test results confidential.
example.zh: 請將這些檢驗結果保密。

note.meaning: 機密的；保密的，不對外公開。

noteEn.meaning: meant to be kept secret, not shared.
noteEn.usage: Often with information or documents; 'keep something confidential'.

noteEs.exampleTr: Por favor, mantén estos resultados en confidencialidad.
noteEs.meaning: secreto; que no se hace público.
noteEs.usage: Va con information o documents; keep sth confidential.

noteHi.exampleTr: कृपया इन जाँच परिणामों को गोपनीय रखें।
noteHi.meaning: गुप्त; जिसे बाहर नहीं बताया जाता।
noteHi.usage: information, documents के साथ; keep sth confidential आम है।

noteJa.exampleTr: これらの検査結果は秘密にしてください。
noteJa.meaning: 秘密の；外部に公開しない。
noteJa.usage: information・documents などを修飾。keep sth confidential の形も多い。

noteKo.exampleTr: 이 검사 결과는 비밀로 해 주세요.
noteKo.usage: information, documents 등을 수식하며 keep sth confidential로도 쓴다.

consent.ex: You need planning consent to build an extension.
consent.zh: 許可；同意（此指規劃許可）

considerably.ex: The new phone is considerably faster.

contend.en: argue or claim something is true
contend.ex: Some experts contend that taxes are too high.

cost.en: the money needed to do or buy something
cost.ex: The cost of living keeps going up.

costs.ex: Rising costs forced the café to close.

court.en: place where legal cases are decided
court.ex: He had to go to court over the accident.

critics.en: people who say something is wrong
critics.ex: Critics say the new law is unfair.

dart.en: name of a Dublin commuter rail service
dart.ja: ダート（ダブリン近郊鉄道）
dart.zh: Dart（都柏林通勤鐵路；Dart+ West 為計畫名）

day.ex: We met on the first day of school.

deal.ex: The two sides reached a deal late at night.

deals.ex: Both sides prefer quick deals to long fights.

defended.en: said something was right when criticised
defended.ex: The minister defended the new tax.

delay.en: a time when something happens later
delay.ex: There was a short delay before take-off.

delays.en: times when things happen later than planned
delays.ex: Snow caused long delays on the roads.

development.ex: A new housing development is planned near the river.

disputes.ex: The neighbours had disputes about the fence.

drainage.en: a system that carries away waste water
drainage.ex: Poor drainage causes flooding in the town.

drawn-out.ex: After a drawn-out debate, they finally voted.

dropped.ex: The charges against him were dropped.

due.en: expected to happen at a set time
due.ex: The train is due at six o'clock.

dundrum.zh: 丹德倫（都柏林南部地區）

earmarked.ex: The council earmarked funds for new parks.
earmarked.ja: 予定された；充てられた

example.en: This field is earmarked for a new school.
example.zh: 這塊地已被指定用來興建新學校。

note.meaning: 指定（土地、資金）作特定用途；預定。
note.usage: 常用被動 be earmarked for sth。

noteEn.meaning: to choose land or money for a particular purpose.

noteEs.exampleTr: Este terreno está destinado a una nueva escuela.
noteEs.meaning: destinar tierras o dinero a un fin concreto.
noteEs.usage: Se usa mucho en pasiva: be earmarked for sth.

noteHi.exampleTr: यह मैदान नए स्कूल के लिए तय किया गया है।
noteHi.meaning: ज़मीन या पैसे को किसी ख़ास काम के लिए तय करना।
noteHi.usage: प्रायः कर्मवाच्य में: be earmarked for sth।

noteJa.exampleTr: この土地は新しい学校の建設予定地だ。
noteJa.meaning: 土地や資金を特定の目的に充てる。
noteJa.usage: 受動態 be earmarked for 〜 でよく使う。

noteKo.exampleTr: 이 땅은 새 학교 부지로 지정되어 있다.
noteKo.usage: 주로 수동태 be earmarked for ~로 쓴다.

effect.en: in effect: in reality, in practice
effect.ex: In effect, the new rule changes nothing.

effectively.ex: The decision effectively ended his career.

elsewhere.ex: Prices are lower elsewhere in the country.

encourage.en: make someone more likely to do something
encourage.ex: Low prices encourage people to buy more.

escalated.ex: Ticket prices escalated during the summer.

example.en: Fuel prices escalated quickly last winter.
example.zh: 去年冬天燃料價格迅速攀升。

note.meaning: （成本、衝突等）逐步升高；急劇增加。
note.usage: 不及物動詞常見：costs escalated；也可指衝突升級 escalate into。

noteEn.meaning: to rise or become worse quickly.
noteEn.usage: Often intransitive: 'costs escalated'; 'escalate into' a bigger problem.

noteEs.exampleTr: Los precios del combustible subieron rápidamente el invierno pasado.
noteEs.usage: Suele ser intransitivo: costs escalated; escalate into = convertirse en.

noteHi.exampleTr: पिछली सर्दियों में ईंधन की कीमतें तेज़ी से बढ़ीं।
noteHi.meaning: लागत या झगड़े का तेज़ी से बढ़ना।
noteHi.usage: costs escalated आम है; escalate into = किसी बड़ी चीज़ में बदलना।

noteJa.exampleTr: 昨冬、燃料価格は急上昇した。
noteJa.meaning: （費用・対立などが）段階的に増大する。
noteJa.usage: costs escalated のように自動詞で多用。escalate into で「〜に発展する」。

noteKo.usage: costs escalated처럼 자동사로 자주 쓰며 escalate into는 '~로 번지다'.

estimated.ex: The estimated cost of the bridge is high.

euro.en: the money used in Ireland and much of Europe

example.en: something that shows what you mean
example.ex: Apples, for example, are rich in fibre.

expensive.ex: That restaurant is too expensive for students.

extend.ex: They plan to extend the bus route to the airport.

extended.ex: She took an extended break from work.

fear.en: worry that something bad will happen
fear.ex: Many workers fear losing their jobs.

fears.en: worries that something bad will happen
fears.ex: The news raised fears of higher prices.

financial.ex: He needs financial help to pay for college.

firm's.ex: The firm's new office is in the city centre.

flagship.en: the most important of a group
flagship.ex: This is the brand's flagship store in London.

floodgates.en: gates holding back water; open the floodgates: let much happen
floodgates.ex: The new rule could open the floodgates to complaints.
floodgates.hi: बाढ़ के द्वार (बड़ी संख्या में मामले खुलना)
floodgates.zh: open the floodgates：打開閘門；引發大量（案件）

for.en: used to show purpose or exchange

funds.ex: The charity raised funds for the hospital.

further.ex: Further details will be posted online.

generated.ex: The film generated a lot of interest.

get.ex: She hopes to get a job in Paris.

go.en: move to a place; go to court: start a case
go.ex: I go to the gym twice a week.

going.en: used to talk about the future
going.ex: It is going to rain tonight.

got.ex: He got a letter from his bank.

greater.en: part of a name: the wider Dublin area
greater.zh: 大（都柏林地區），名稱一部分

grew.ex: The town grew quickly after the factory opened.

had.en: used to form the past perfect

handing.en: giving money or things to someone
handing.ex: He is handing over the keys tomorrow.

hardware.ex: I bought nails at the hardware shop.

has.en: used to form the present perfect

hearing.en: a meeting of a court to hear a case
hearing.ex: The hearing was put off until May.

hefty.ex: He paid a hefty fine for speeding.

high.en: part of the name High Court

homes.en: houses or flats where people live
homes.ex: The city needs more affordable homes.

hope.en: a wish for something to happen
hope.ex: She moved abroad in the hope of a better life.
hope.zh: 希望（in the hope of：希望能…）

house.ex: Their house has a big garden.

houses.ex: Old houses line the quiet street.

however.en: but; used to add a contrast
however.ex: The plan is good; however, it is expensive.

illustrative.ex: This case is illustrative of a wider problem.
illustrative.zh: 具說明性的；可作例證的

incentivise.ex: Lower fees could incentivise more people to cycle.

example.en: Tax breaks incentivise companies to hire young workers.
example.zh: 減稅措施激勵公司雇用年輕員工。

note.meaning: 用獎勵或好處激勵（某人做某事）。
note.usage: incentivise sb to do sth；英式拼法 -ise，美式為 incentivize。

noteEn.meaning: to make someone want to do something by offering a reward.
noteEn.usage: Use 'incentivise someone to do something'; US spelling is incentivize.

noteEs.exampleTr: Las rebajas fiscales incentivan a las empresas a contratar jóvenes.
noteEs.meaning: motivar a alguien ofreciendo una recompensa o ventaja.
noteEs.usage: incentivise sb to do sth; en EE. UU. se escribe incentivize.

noteHi.exampleTr: कर छूट कंपनियों को युवा कर्मचारी रखने के लिए प्रेरित करती है।
noteHi.meaning: इनाम या लाभ देकर किसी को कुछ करने के लिए प्रेरित करना।
noteHi.usage: incentivise sb to do sth; अमेरिकी वर्तनी incentivize है।

noteJa.exampleTr: 減税は企業に若者の採用を促す。
noteJa.meaning: 報酬や利益を与えて何かをするよう促す。
noteJa.usage: incentivise sb to do sth の形。米式綴りは incentivize。

noteKo.exampleTr: 세금 감면은 기업이 젊은 직원을 채용하도록 장려한다.
noteKo.meaning: 보상이나 이익을 주어 어떤 행동을 하도록 장려하다.
noteKo.usage: incentivise sb to do sth 형태; 미국식 철자는 incentivize.

indicate.ex: The results indicate a clear rise in demand.

individuals.ex: The tax affects individuals and companies.

inflate.ex: Late changes can inflate building costs.
inflate.ja: 膨らませる；つり上げる

infrastructure.en: roads, railways and basic public systems
infrastructure.ex: The country needs to invest in its infrastructure.

example.en: Good transport infrastructure helps a city grow.
example.zh: 良好的交通基礎建設有助城市發展。

note.meaning: 基礎建設；道路、鐵路、供水等公共設施。
note.usage: 多為不可數名詞；常作修飾語，如 infrastructure projects。

noteEn.meaning: basic public systems like roads, railways and water supply.
noteEn.usage: Usually uncountable; often used before another noun, e.g. infrastructure projects.

noteEs.exampleTr: Una buena infraestructura de transporte ayuda a crecer a una ciudad.
noteEs.meaning: carreteras, trenes, agua y otros servicios públicos básicos.
noteEs.usage: Suele ser incontable; aparece en infrastructure projects.

noteHi.exampleTr: अच्छा परिवहन ढांचा शहर के विकास में मदद करता है।
noteHi.meaning: सड़क, रेल, पानी जैसी बुनियादी सार्वजनिक सुविधाएँ।
noteHi.usage: प्रायः अगणनीय; infrastructure projects जैसे संयोजन आम हैं।

noteJa.exampleTr: 優れた交通インフラは都市の成長を助ける。
noteJa.meaning: 道路・鉄道・水道などの社会基盤。
noteJa.usage: 通常は不可算。infrastructure projects のように修飾語でも使う。

noteKo.exampleTr: 좋은 교통 기반 시설은 도시 성장에 도움이 된다.
noteKo.meaning: 도로, 철도, 수도 같은 기본 공공 시설.
noteKo.usage: 주로 불가산 명사이며 infrastructure projects처럼 수식어로도 쓴다.

initiate.ex: The council will initiate a review of bus fares.

irish.en: from Ireland; part of the name Irish Rail

judicial.ex: Judges must stay independent in judicial matters.

june.en: the sixth month of the year

launch.ex: They plan to launch a new campaign in May.

leading.ex: Heavy rain is leading to floods in the north.

legal.ex: She asked a lawyer for legal advice.

less.en: a smaller amount; not as much
less.ex: This laptop costs less than mine.

line.ex: The new tram line opens next year.

litigation.ex: The company faces years of costly litigation.

example.en: Both firms wanted to avoid expensive litigation.
example.zh: 兩家公司都想避免昂貴的訴訟。

note.meaning: 訴訟；透過法院解決爭端的過程。
note.usage: 不可數名詞，常見於正式或法律語境；engage in / face litigation。

noteEn.meaning: the process of taking a disagreement to court.
noteEn.usage: Uncountable and formal; common in legal and business writing.

noteEs.exampleTr: Ambas empresas querían evitar un litigio costoso.
noteEs.meaning: proceso de resolver un conflicto en los tribunales.
noteEs.usage: Sustantivo incontable y formal; se usa en contextos legales.

noteHi.exampleTr: दोनों कंपनियाँ महँगी मुकदमेबाज़ी से बचना चाहती थीं।
noteHi.meaning: अदालत में मुकदमा लड़ने की प्रक्रिया।
noteHi.usage: अगणनीय संज्ञा; औपचारिक और कानूनी संदर्भ में प्रयोग।

noteJa.exampleTr: 両社とも費用のかかる訴訟を避けたかった。
noteJa.usage: 不可算名詞で、法律・ビジネスの硬い文脈で使う。

noteKo.exampleTr: 두 회사 모두 비용이 많이 드는 소송을 피하고 싶었다.

long.ex: We had a long wait at the airport.

lot.en: a lot of: a large amount
lot.ex: She drinks a lot of tea.

made.en: made a deal: reached an agreement
made.ex: They made a deal to share the costs.

maintained.en: said firmly that something is true
maintained.ex: He maintained that he had done nothing wrong.

major.ex: The city is planning major road works.

maynooth.zh: 梅努斯（基爾代爾郡城鎮）

metro.en: an underground train system in a city
metro.ex: I take the metro to work every day.

metrolink.en: a planned metro line in Dublin

money.en: coins and notes used to buy things
money.ex: She saves money for a holiday.

much.en: a large amount; as much as = up to

navan.en: part of the name Navan Road, a Dublin street
navan.zh: Navan Road：納凡路（都柏林西部道路）

nevertheless.ex: It was raining; nevertheless, we went out.

new.ex: They opened a new library in town.

notable.ex: The city has several notable buildings.

objecting.en: saying formally you do not agree
objecting.ex: Many residents are objecting to the new road.

objectors.en: people who formally oppose a plan
objectors.ex: Objectors say the tower is too tall.

official.en: a person with an important job in government
official.ex: A government official answered our questions.

open.ex: The new shop will open on Monday.

opportunistic.en: using a chance for selfish gain
opportunistic.ex: Opportunistic sellers raised prices during the storm.

example.en: Critics called the price rise purely opportunistic.
example.zh: 批評者稱這次漲價純屬趁火打劫。

note.meaning: 投機的；機會主義的，趁機謀私利。
note.usage: 帶貶義，常修飾 behaviour、litigation、attack 等名詞。

noteEn.meaning: using a chance to get an unfair advantage.
noteEn.usage: Negative; used with nouns like behaviour, litigation or attack.

noteEs.exampleTr: Los críticos calificaron la subida de precios de puramente oportunista.
noteEs.meaning: que aprovecha una ocasión para beneficio propio.
noteEs.usage: Tiene sentido negativo; va con behaviour o litigation.

noteHi.exampleTr: आलोचकों ने कीमत बढ़ाने को पूरी तरह अवसरवादी कहा।
noteHi.meaning: मौक़े का फ़ायदा उठाकर स्वार्थ साधने वाला।
noteHi.usage: नकारात्मक अर्थ; behaviour, litigation जैसे शब्दों के साथ।

noteJa.exampleTr: 批判者はその値上げを単なる便乗だと言った。
noteJa.meaning: 機会に乗じて私利を図る。
noteJa.usage: 否定的な語。behaviour・litigation などを修飾する。

noteKo.exampleTr: 비판자들은 가격 인상이 순전히 기회주의적이라고 했다.
noteKo.usage: 부정적인 뜻으로 behaviour, litigation 등을 수식한다.

out.ex: She had to shell out for a new car.

over.ex: Please hand over your tickets at the door.

paid.ex: We paid fifty euro for the tickets.

paying.ex: They are paying too much for rent.

payments.ex: Monthly payments on the loan are €300.

payouts.en: large sums of money paid out
payouts.ex: Insurance payouts rose after the floods.

people.ex: Many people walk to work here.

permission.en: official agreement to let you do something
permission.ex: You need permission to park here.

plan.en: an idea or arrangement for the future
plan.ex: The council has a plan for a new park.

planned.en: arranged to happen in the future
planned.ex: A new school is planned for the area.

planning.ex: Planning rules limit the height of new buildings.

point.ex: The facts point to a simple mistake.

price.en: the money needed to buy something
price.ex: The price of bread has gone up.

project.en: a large planned piece of work
project.ex: The bridge project will take three years.

projects.ex: The city has several building projects this year.

prominent.ex: She is a prominent lawyer in the city.

prompting.ex: The news is prompting calls for change.

properties.en: buildings and land owned by someone
properties.ex: Property prices are rising fast in the suburbs.

proposed.ex: Locals oppose the proposed wind farm.

prospective.en: likely to become something in the future

protracted.ex: After protracted talks, they finally agreed.

example.en: The strike led to protracted talks with the union.
example.zh: 罷工導致與工會進行了漫長的談判。

note.meaning: 拖得很久的；曠日持久的（通常帶負面意味）。
note.usage: 多修飾 talks、dispute、negotiations、delays 等名詞，暗示時間過長。

noteEn.meaning: lasting much longer than expected or wanted.
noteEn.usage: Used before nouns like talks, dispute and delays; sounds negative.

noteEs.exampleTr: La huelga provocó largas negociaciones con el sindicato.
noteEs.meaning: que dura mucho más de lo esperado.
noteEs.usage: Acompaña a talks, dispute o delays; tiene tono negativo.

noteHi.exampleTr: हड़ताल के कारण यूनियन के साथ लंबी बातचीत चली।
noteHi.meaning: ज़रूरत से ज़्यादा लंबा खिंचने वाला।
noteHi.usage: talks, dispute, delays जैसे शब्दों के साथ, नकारात्मक भाव में।

noteJa.exampleTr: ストライキのため組合との交渉は長引いた。
noteJa.usage: talks・dispute・delays などと結びつき、否定的な響きがある。

noteKo.usage: talks, dispute, delays 등과 함께 부정적인 뜻으로 쓰인다.

paragraphs: The State is paying a lot of money to some people who go to court against big building projects. Some people call this "ransom" money.

One company in west Dublin went to court against a new train project. The project costs about €1 billion. On the day of the court case, the train company made a secret deal with it. The case stopped. The company got about €10.9 million.
The State also bought houses from people who were against a new metro line and new homes. It paid €2 million or more for each house.
An official says deals cost less than long delays. But some people are worried. They think more people will go to court to get money.
State bodies are paying large amounts of money to people who go to court to stop big building projects. Some people are worried that the State is paying "ransom" money.

In one case, a hardware company on the Navan Road in west Dublin went to court against Dart+ West. This €1 billion project will bring more trains to Maynooth and Dunboyne. On the day the case was going to start in the High Court in June 2025, Irish Rail said it had made a secret deal with the company. The case stopped. The company's accounts show it got about €10.9 million.
The State also bought houses from people who were against the MetroLink line in Dublin and a plan for about 1,000 new homes in Dundrum. It paid €2 million or more for each house.

A senior official said a deal is cheaper than a long delay. Delays can add hundreds of millions of euro to costs. For example, a Dublin drainage project grew from about €500 million to as much as €2.3 billion after years of arguments.
But some people warn that these payments may make more people go to court to get money.
State bodies are paying large sums of money to people who take court challenges against major infrastructure projects, leading to concerns that they are paying "ransom" to objectors.

In one case, a hardware wholesaler on the Navan Road in west Dublin challenged planning permission for Dart+ West, a project worth about €1 billion to extend rail services to Maynooth and Dunboyne. On the day the case was due in the High Court in June 2025, Irish Rail announced a confidential settlement, and the challenge was withdrawn. The company's accounts suggest it received about €10.9 million in total.
In other cases, the State bought homes from people objecting to the MetroLink line and to around 1,000 new homes planned in Dundrum, paying €2 million or more for each.

A senior official said settling is cheaper than long delays, which can add hundreds of millions to costs. The Greater Dublin Drainage scheme, for example, rose from about €500 million to as much as €2.3 billion after years of disputes.
However, critics warn that such payments could encourage more people to go to court in the hope of a deal.
State agencies are handing over hefty sums to individuals who launch legal challenges against flagship infrastructure projects, prompting fears that the public purse is effectively paying "ransom".

In a notable case, a hardware wholesaler on Dublin's Navan Road sought a judicial review of the planning consent for Dart+ West, a roughly €1 billion scheme to extend rail services to Maynooth and Dunboyne. On the very day the case was set to open in the High Court in June 2025, Irish Rail unveiled a confidential settlement and the challenge was dropped. The firm's accounts point to a windfall of some €10.9 million.
Elsewhere, the State has snapped up homes belonging to objectors to the MetroLink line and to some 1,000 homes earmarked for Dundrum, shelling out upwards of €2 million apiece.

One senior official defended the approach, reasoning that a settlement comes cheaper than protracted delays, which can inflate costs by hundreds of millions. The Greater Dublin Drainage scheme is a cautionary tale: its price tag ballooned from around €500 million to as much as €2.3 billion amid drawn-out disputes.
Critics, however, fear the payouts could open the floodgates to opportunistic litigation.

In one prominent case, a hardware wholesaler on the Navan Road in west Dublin sought a judicial review of the planning approval for Dart+ West, a project valued at approximately €1 billion that will extend rail services to Maynooth and Dunboyne. The company's financial statements indicate that it received approximately €10.9 million.
In comparable cases, the State has acquired properties from objectors to the MetroLink line and to a proposed development of around 1,000 homes in Dundrum, paying €2 million or more for each.

A senior official maintained that settlement is considerably less expensive than prolonged delays, which can increase costs by hundreds of millions. The Greater Dublin Drainage scheme is illustrative: its estimated cost escalated from approximately €500 million to as much as €2.3 billion following extended disputes.
Nevertheless, critics contend that such payments may incentivise further litigation, as prospective objectors may anticipate a financial settlement.
